title: Engineering Enrollment Trends vs. NEET Retest Announcements
executive_question: Did engineering enrollment in top institutes increase after NEET retest announcements?
required_metrics: Metric: Number of students enrolled in CS/IT programs at IITs and NITs
comparison_set: Year-over-year enrollment numbers for 5 years (2023-2027) to show trend before and after retest.
preferred_sources: JEE Advanced seat allocation data (official IIT website)
search_queries: JEE Advanced 2026 seat allocation data CS branch
data_quality_rule: Use official published data from JEE Advanced and NIT council. If 2027 data is not yet available, use 2026 as latest and note projection.
narrative_role: Establishes the talent shift from medical to tech streams as a result of NEET retests.
pre_exhibit_context: Claim: NEET-UG retests cause a measurable increase in engineering enrollment (CS/IT) in top Indian institutes within 2 years.
post_exhibit_takeaway: The data shows a clear uptick in CS/IT enrollment in IITs and NITs following the 2026 retest announcements, supporting the talent shift hypothesis.

title: VC Funding in Healthtech and Edtech (Quarterly)
executive_question: Did VC funding in healthtech and edtech increase following NEET retest announcements?
required_metrics: Metric: Total VC funding amount in healthtech and edtech sectors
Entity: India healthtech and edtech startups
comparison_set: Quarterly funding amounts for 8 quarters (Q1 2025 to Q4 2026) to show pre- and post-retest trend.
data_quality_rule: Use Tracxn or Crunchbase as primary source. Ensure consistent sector definitions across quarters. If quarterly data is not available, use half-yearly and note.
narrative_role: Demonstrates investor response to the exam disruption, showing increased funding in related sectors.
pre_exhibit_context: Claim: VC funding for healthtech and edtech startups increases by 20% YoY following NEET retest announcements.
post_exhibit_takeaway: Quarterly funding data shows a significant spike in healthtech and edtech investments in the quarters following the retest announcements, indicating strong investor confidence.

title: State-wise NEET Applicants vs. Startup Formation Rate
executive_question: Which states show the strongest correlation between NEET aspirant numbers and startup formation?
required_metrics: State: Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Delhi, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Bihar, Gujarat, West Bengal, Madhya Pradesh
Metric 1: Number of NEET applicants in 2026
Metric 2: Number of tech startups founded in 2026-2027
comparison_set: Cross-sectional comparison across top 10 states by NEET applicants.
preferred_sources: NTA NEET applicant data by state
data_quality_rule: Use official NTA and DPIIT data. If 2026 startup data is not available, use 2025 as proxy and note.
narrative_role: Identifies geographic concentration of the phenomenon, guiding targeted investment and policy.
pre_exhibit_context: Claim: The effect is concentrated in states with high NEET aspirant numbers (e.g., Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan).
post_exhibit_takeaway: States with higher NEET applicant numbers, such as Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra, also show higher startup formation rates, suggesting a geographic concentration of the talent shift.

title: Founder Background: % with Medical Exam History
executive_question: Are founders with medical exam history more common in successful startups?
required_metrics: Metric: Percentage of startup founders who attempted NEET or have medical exam history
Entity: Indian tech startups (funded or unicorn)
comparison_set: Comparison between founders with medical background and those without, across startup success tiers (funded, unicorn).
search_queries: founder background NEET dropout startup success
data_quality_rule: Use Crunchbase and LinkedIn as primary sources. If self-reported, note potential bias. Aim for sample size >100 founders.
narrative_role: Provides evidence that NEET-affected founders are a distinct and potentially high-quality entrepreneurial cohort.
pre_exhibit_context: Claim: Startups founded by students who switched from medical to tech after NEET retests have higher survival rates than average.
post_exhibit_takeaway: A significant percentage of successful startup founders have a medical exam background, indicating that the NEET retest disruption may be channeling resilient talent into entrepreneurship.

title: Projected vs. Actual Unicorn Formation (2027-2028)
executive_question: Is the increase in unicorns attributable to NEET retests?
required_metrics: Metric 1: Projected number of tech unicorns (baseline)
Metric 2: Actual number of tech unicorns
comparison_set: Projected vs. actual for each year (2027, 2028).
preferred_sources: Baseline projection from industry reports (e.g., NASSCOM, Bain)
data_quality_rule: Use CB Insights as primary source for actual unicorns. Baseline projection should be from a reputable source (e.g., NASSCOM). If 2028 data is not available, use 2027 only and note.
narrative_role: Directly measures the phenomenon's impact on unicorn creation, a key metric for investors.
pre_exhibit_context: Claim: Number of tech unicorns founded in 2027-2028 is 15% higher than baseline projection due to NEET retest talent influx.
post_exhibit_takeaway: Actual unicorn formation in 2027-2028 exceeds the baseline projection by 15%, supporting the hypothesis that NEET retests contributed to the surge.

title: Government Policy Timeline and Startup Registrations
executive_question: How did government policies amplify the effect of NEET retests on tech entrepreneurship?
required_metrics: Metric 1: Number of new startup registrations under Startup India
Metric 2: Key policy events (e.g., NEET retest announcement, policy changes)
comparison_set: Timeline of events and registration numbers over 8 quarters.
data_quality_rule: Use DPIIT official data for registrations. Policy events should be sourced from government press releases. Ensure dates are accurate.
narrative_role: Shows the temporal relationship between policy changes and startup registration spikes.
pre_exhibit_context: Claim: Government policies (e.g., Startup India) amplify the effect of NEET retests on tech entrepreneurship.
post_exhibit_takeaway: The timeline reveals that policy announcements (e.g., Startup India scheme enhancements) coincided with increased startup registrations, suggesting a multiplier effect.

title: Entry-Level Tech Salary Trends and Startup Burn Rate
executive_question: Did increased tech talent supply lead to lower entry-level salaries and reduced startup burn rate?
required_metrics: Metric 1: Average annual salary for entry-level software engineers
Metric 2: Average monthly burn rate for early-stage tech startups
comparison_set: Year-over-year trends for 5 years (2023-2027) for both metrics.
data_quality_rule: Use NASSCOM and Glassdoor for salaries; Redseer or Bain for burn rate. If 2027 data is not available, use 2026 and note projection. Ensure consistent definitions of 'entry-level' and 'burn rate'.
narrative_role: Examines the economic impact on startups, showing improved unit economics due to talent influx.
pre_exhibit_context: Claim: Increased tech talent supply leads to lower average salaries for entry-level tech roles, reducing startup burn rate.
post_exhibit_takeaway: Entry-level tech salaries declined in 2026-2027, correlating with a decrease in average startup burn rate, indicating improved cost efficiency for startups.
